key_insight: Hyper-reduction targets localized nonlinear corrections to accelerate coupled elastoplastic soil deformation and water-flow simulations while retaining high accuracy.
engineering_relevance: Faster repeated dam simulations can support parameter calibration, uncertainty quantification and safety scenario analysis.
method: Build separate displacement and pore-pressure reduced bases using proper orthogonal decomposition.
Compute affine residual terms exactly and approximate nonlinear corrections with ECSW cubature, one rule per balance equation.
Assemble the original FEniCSx variational forms only on selected elements.
evidence_signal: Tests on 2D and 3D dams undergoing raising and consolidation reported displacement and pressure errors below 0.5% relative to finite element solutions, with speed-ups up to 43× and 77×, respectively.
watch_item: Accuracy beyond the tested parameter ranges and loading scenarios is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: A hyper-reduction strategy for elastoplastic hydro-mechanical problems in partially saturated soil
